name: Shimei
overview: Shimei was a male Levite known for having married a foreign wife, a fact recorded in the book of Ezra. His identity as a Levite places him within the tribe entrusted with religious duties in Israel. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimei means 'YHWH has heard' or 'famous' in Hebrew. This proper name reflects a common theophoric element referencing God's attentiveness or renown, though the name itself was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shimei as a descendant of Levi, confirming his tribal lineage. No further family relationships are recorded beyond his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Shimei's mention highlights the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenantal purity, particularly concerning intermarriage. His marriage to a foreign wife signifies a point of concern addressed in Ezra's reforms, emphasizing the community's call to faithfulness to God's commands. Thus, Shimei serves as a representative example of the Levites who needed to align their lives with God's covenant during the restoration period.
